When an interface is brought back up
column2: the kernel tries to restore the

column1: host routes tied to its permanent addresses.
However
column2: if the host route was removed from the FIB

column1: reinsert it. This is done by releasing the current dst and allocating a
new
column2: so as to not reuse a dst with obsolete values.

column1: Since this function is called under RTNL and using the same explanation
from the previous patch
column2: we can test if the route is in the FIB by

column1: checking its node pointer instead of its reference count.
Tested using the following script and Andrey's reproducer mentioned
in commit 8048ced9beb2 (""net: ipv6: regenerate host route if moved to gc
list"") and linked below:
$ ip link set dev lo up
$ ip link add dummy1 type dummy
$ ip -6 address add cafe::1/64 dev dummy1
$ ip link set dev lo down	# cafe::1/128 is removed
$ ip link set dev dummy1 up
$ ip link set dev lo up
The host route is correctly regenerated.
